indicators.note: rejecting something throws it back, so the word for students is read backwards

parts.note: students are pupils

explanation.surface: A college turns down applicants and admits it got it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless error or blunder is informally called this hyphenated term.

clue.text: Some moped, a lovely recreational form of transport

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone admires a lovely moped as a fun way to get about.
explanation.definitionFit: A small foot-powered boat hired for fun on lakes and at the seaside is a leisure vehicle.

clue.text: Old Austrian coin about to waste away? Scary!

indicators.note: about means the coin's letters are placed around the next piece

parts.note: the schilling was Austria's currency before the euro
to pine is to waste away with longing

explanation.surface: An old Austrian coin is about to wither away, which sounds frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the signal that the coin goes round the word for waste away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something terrifying sends a shiver down the back, so frightening fits.

indicators.note: turned over says the letters of the preceding words are flipped end to end

parts.note: to run something, such as a team, is to lead it; past tense led

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper confesses the shop they ran went bust.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling cooked meats and prepared foods.

clue.text: Madman taking one drug after another

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis, another drug

explanation.surface: A lunatic is using one drug after another.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric or crazy person is called this, informally.

clue.text: Oily substance male put on wood

indicators.note: put on means the first piece is added onto the end of the second

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood

explanation.surface: A man rubs oil onto a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm or resin given off by certain plants is an aromatic oily substance.

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and can mean with, as in fish and chips

explanation.surface: Someone makes a mess of a household task.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip to do a task, such as picking up shopping, is a small job.

indicators.note: shenanigans are mischievous goings-on, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: New Year's Eve high jinks take place in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown tropical hardwood used in fine furniture.

indicators.note: the apostrophe in front of the word marks an H dropped from speech, so the synonym loses its H the same way

parts.note: with its H restored, hirsute means hairy

explanation.surface: A Cockney-style speaker asks whether something fine and dainty is hairy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe marks the missing H, as in Cockney speech, so the synonym of hirsute also drops its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy is light, breezy and delicate in texture or manner.

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician and a crooked despot both refuse to admit anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges DICTATOR and IN into TRADICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Contradicting a statement is saying the opposite, a denial of it.

clue.text: Junior clergyman, company welcomed by senior clergyman

indicators.note: welcomed by means the company is taken inside the senior churchman

parts.note: a dean heads a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A lowly cleric and his friends are received by a superior.
explanation.definitionFit: This ordained minister ranks below a priest in many churches.

clue.text: Country absolutely not accepting Russian capital

indicators.note: accepting means the refusal takes the letter into its middle

parts.note: no way is an emphatic refusal

indicators.note: the capital, or initial letter, of the word Russian

explanation.surface: A nation flatly refuses to welcome Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian capital' looks like Moscow, but it is just the capital letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian kingdom whose capital is Oslo.

clue.text: Pass by circuit, borders of Silverstone

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A racing driver overtakes during a lap at Silverstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverstone is a British motor-racing circuit, home of the British Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, time or a right that lapses comes to an end, expires or passes.

parts.note: Peter Pan is the boy who never grew up
ties means fastens

explanation.surface: A boy who never ages does up his undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Short knickers worn by women and girls are a type of undergarment.

clue.text: Image to choose, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks whether this is how the word is spoken

parts.note: to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone checks they heard right that they should select a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal shortening of picture, meaning a photograph or image.

clue.text: Greek character in recent times collecting stamps

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lately means in recent times

explanation.surface: A Greek man has recently taken up a hobby with postage.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobby of collecting and studying postage stamps has this formal name.

parts.note: a dale is a valley

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A gloomy valley holds something without a soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daleks are the emotionless cyborg villains of the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who's robotic enemies are heartless mutants in metal casings, a fitting description.

parts.note: ... green is a traditional bright green cloth, and the same name belongs to a famous American president

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded American leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests ecology, but it is the shade worn by Robin Hood's men, named after an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a famous American president also names a shade of green cloth.

definitions.meaning: a host asks a guest to visit once more
an informal request to repeat what was just said

explanation.surface: A guest is invited back but doesn't catch the words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both asks a visitor back and asks a speaker to repeat themselves, like pardon.

clue.text: Besieged religious outpost on outskirts of Delaware, fashionable

parts.note: the Alamo was a Texan mission besieged in 1836

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A historic siege site stands at the edge of an American state that's in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning in the current fashion, stylish.

definitions.meaning: a scorching day is informally called a scorcher or ...
a bird suitable for cooking in the oven

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sweltering day suits a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a very hot day and a fowl reared for oven cooking.

clue.text: Work on minor spasm of the eye

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone tries to treat a twitch in their eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to vision or the eye, as in the optic nerve.

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Someone sure about fortified wine and German wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the fortified wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish red from the region of the same name in northern Spain.

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a Finn is a native of Finland

explanation.surface: A European pub has lost its roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or small hotel offering drink and lodging.
